customs_officer.text: The Custom House, 1681. Every bale of cloth and every barrel of wine that came up the canal paid its duty in this room.
The ceilings upstairs are ornate plasterwork, very showy. Exeter's merchants wanted the world to know the wool trade was going well.

In the 1200s Isabella de Fortibus, Countess of Devon, built a weir across the river, and later the Earls of Devon blocked it further so their own town of Topsham got the trade. Exeter was cut off from the sea. It took three hundred years and a canal to sort it out. That's Devon for you.
